pr_title: gpio_emul: Fix bug with input & output pins
pr_body:
Change gpio_emul_input_set_masked_pend to log when it returns an error.
Changed all calls to gpio_emul_input_set_masked* to check the return
value.

Added a test case that sets and reads emulated 2 gpios to make sure
they don't interact with each other. Fails before this cl, passes
afterwards.

./scripts/twister -T tests/drivers/gpio

The function gpio_emul_input_set_masked_pend will not set the input
values if there are bits set in the value that are not in the mask. In
almost every call to that function, the value wasn't being limited to
bits set in the mask, so they were failing if there was more than one
gpio configured for INPUT|OUTPUT with a value of 1.
pr_comments:
> The function gpio_emul_input_set_masked_pend will not set the input values if there are bits set in the value that are not in the mask.

My originally implementation operated the way you describe but I was asked to change it so that it would set bits regardless of what the mask was, because it reflected more closely what actual hardware does.

Generally, GPIO-oriented registers may return values that fall outside of the provided mask. E.g. an application is perfectly OK to use a mask of (-1) to refer to all pins, regardless of which are actually in use, and that should not trigger an error.

So currently, I do not believe this change is correct or required.

cc: @pabigot

>

That is why I added the new test, which fails without my changes. The test demonstrates that the code does not work as intended.

If you called gpio_emul_input_set_masked_pend with a mask of -1 and a value of 3, that would work fine. However if you call it with a mask of 3 and a value of -1, it will return an error, which is exactly what the code in 

> Can you please remove the added log messages and whitespace changes? It would be easier to review if the change only reflected what the minimal necessary changes.

There are no whitespace changes, so I don't understand what you mean.  The only "whitespace" changes are where the line was <80 chars, I added text making it over 80 chars, and so I wrapped it. These are the minimal necessary changes.

> 
> Additionally, why was it necessary to modify the test suite?

I added a new test to prove that the code was not working correctly, and the test passes after my changes to prove that they work.

> However if you call it with a mask of 3 and a value of -1, it will return an error, which is exactly what the code in

I'm not active with Zephyr, but my recollection was the design was intended to allow -1 to be passed as a mask meaning "all pins, even if some are missing" but also as a value meaning "set all pins even if they're outside of the mask".  So it sounds to me like the code is wrong.

I don't know.  At the time I was working GPIO, that (i.e. returning an error) would be the wrong thing to do.  Other GPIO drivers from that time wouldn't treat that as an error.  What do they do now?  An emulator should generally behave like others; if real hardware rejects the combination so should the emulator.

Though IIRC the "emulator" infrastructure is a little unusual, so if this is in a function that is invoked by emulator-specific code that instructs the emulator how to behave, rather than in code that's reached using GPIO driver functions, an error might be appropriate.

I defer to @cfriedt to figure out the best overall approach.

> Though IIRC the "emulator" infrastructure is a little unusual, so if this is in a function that is invoked by emulator-specific code that instructs the emulator how to behave, rather than in code that's reached using GPIO driver functions, an error might be appropriate.

In this case, my problems are in emulator code calling other emulator code and passing data which causes errors and ignoring those error codes. So my change ignores whether it is proper to return errors and always passes data that won't cause errors instead. I also changed the code to not ignore the errors, in case something like this comes up again.

> I defer to @cfriedt to figure out the best overall approach.

A good test would be to compare against a few different hardware platforms and report results here.

Also, it would be great if @mnkp could weigh in as the current GPIO maintainer.

Ultimately, `gpio_emul` must be consistent with non-emulated hardware.

> Ultimately, `gpio_emul` must be consistent with non-emulated hardware.

I can guarantee there is no hardware that lets you set one output gpio and read the value back, but if you set 2 output gpios, the 2nd one reads as 0.  That is the current behavior of the emulator.
@mnkp I made the changes you requested. Please take another look. The test still passes.

issue_context.title: Can't read more than one OUTPUT|INPUT gpio pin in gpio_emul
issue_context.body:
Calling gpio_emul_driver->port_set_bits_raw() to enable a OUTPUT|INPUT pin, followed by gpio_emul_driver->port_get_raw() to read that same pin would return 0 for the value if there were any other GPIO output pins also set to 1.

This is only a problem in the gpio_emul, not in the gpio driver itself.
